### 2026-07-14: Memory planning vs zero-copy views

**By:** Sapper

**What:** **Change LATER, not now.** Today's allocator needs **no change for
correctness** — the conservative whole-run `pinned` set is sound. The rules
below become mandatory the moment a real liveness/interval-based memory
planner (the ORT-style "share one physical buffer across values with
disjoint lifetimes" optimization in `docs/architecture/ORT2.md §8`, currently design-only
`todo!()` — there is no `onnx-runtime-memory` crate yet) lands.

**Why (grounded in `crates/onnx-runtime-session/src/executor.rs`):**

Today "memory planning" is **per-value allocation + shape-keyed reuse +
conservative pinning** — there is NO cross-value buffer sharing, no
liveness-interval reuse, no in-place donation:

- `buffers: HashMap<ValueId, DeviceBuffer>` — exactly one physical buffer per
  backed value, keyed by `ValueId`, held for the executor's whole life
  (`Drop` at 2036-2042). Static values sized once at build (`size_buffers`
  702-715 via the build path 625-630); dynamic values sized per run and
  **reused only when the resolved shape is byte-identical** (`ensure_buffer`
  636-651: `buffer_shapes[vid] == dims → reuse`, else dealloc+realloc; output
  path 1152-1177 uses the same `b.len() == need` gate).
- `relu_in_place` (ep-cpu) is intra-kernel on a kernel-local buffer — it is
  **not** cross-value buffer donation. No session-level in-place aliasing
  exists.

Views layer cleanly on top of that model:
- A view value owns no buffer; it is recorded in `views: HashMap<ValueId,
  ValueView{source, shape, strides, byte_offset}>` (211, 225-230) and its
  buffer (if it had one from a prior run) is **removed + freed** when it
  becomes a view (1129-1132). Views are flattened to a single hop, so
  `source`/`root_of` (1376-1381) is always a real buffer owner.
- `pinned: HashSet<ValueId>` holds every **source** value with ≥1 live view
  alias (1142). A pinned buffer "must not be reused or deallocated for the
  remainder of the run" (212-216). It is enforced at the only two places a
  buffer can be freed/resized mid-run — the view-output producer path
  (`debug_assert !pinned.contains(&ovid)` 1124-1131) and the compute-output
  resize path (1166-1173).
- **Why pinning is sufficient today:** `pinned` gates value ids, and under SSA
  topological order a view's producer node consumes its source, so the source
  is produced strictly before any viewer — a source can never be "reproduced
  or resized while pinned" within a run (the debug_asserts document an
  unreachable case, not a live guard). Nothing else frees a buffer mid-run:
  the compute path only ever removes/reallocs the value it is currently
  producing (1152-1177, 1249-1281), never an arbitrary source. `views`/
  `pinned` are cleared at the top of every `run_scoped` (868-869), so no view
  metadata leaks across runs where buffers may be resized. Boundaries copy:
  graph outputs (`contiguous_bytes` 1387-1424 via 930) and control-flow scope
  captures (`materialize_scope` 1466-1480 → `value_tensor` → `contiguous_bytes`)
  gather the view into fresh owned bytes, so no view ever crosses into a child
  executor or out to the DLPack boundary. Strided-unaware consumers gather
  into a private temp (1179-1211). The result: **no path can free or reuse a
  source buffer while a view aliases it.**

**Rules for the future liveness planner (each MUST hold):**

1. **Views own no slot — exclude them from allocation.** A value in `views`
   must never be assigned a physical buffer/arena slot. It is a
   `(source_slot, shape, strides, byte_offset)` descriptor. (The producer path
   already frees any owned buffer at 1129-1132; the planner's interval builder
   must simply skip view values.)

2. **Fold view uses into the source's live interval (THE critical rule).** A
   source's `last_use` = max over (its own direct consumers) **and every
   transitive view alias's last_use**. A view read at schedule step *t* extends
   its source's interval to at least *t*. Because views flatten to one hop
   (`root_of`), this is a single union over `{ovid : views[ovid].source ==
   src}` — but it MUST include materialization reads too (graph-output collect,
   control-flow capture, strided-unaware gather), each of which reads the
   source through the view.

3. **A slot with a live view alias is non-donatable / non-overwritable.** No
   in-place op may donate a source's slot to another value, and no other value
   may be colored into that slot, while any view alias's interval is live. This
   generalizes today's binary whole-run `pinned` to **interval-granular
   pinning**: pin the *slot* for `[source.first_use, extended_last_use]` rather
   than the *value id* for the whole run.

4. **Materialization points allocate fresh slots.** Every gather —
   strided-unaware consumer temp (1183-1211), graph-output collection (930),
   control-flow scope capture — produces a NEW contiguous buffer with its own
   (short) interval. The planner must size and color these, not assume the view
   is free at the boundary.

5. **Reconcile with shape-keyed per-run reuse + symbolic shapes.** The existing
   `ensure_buffer` shape-keyed cache (636-651) and any static AOT plan must
   agree on ownership: a value that is a view on run N owns no slot on run N but
   may own one on run N+1 (data-dependent view-vs-copy, e.g. Slice falling back
   to copy for sub-byte dtypes). The interval plan must be recomputed (or
   guarded) whenever the view-vs-owner decision or a symbolic extent changes —
   never cache a slot assignment across a run whose view topology differs.

**Perf note (Q3):** Whole-run pinning is conservative and *does* leave
performance on the table for a future arena — pinning a large activation
source for the entire run can retain it long after its last real read, raising
peak arena residency. For **decoder graphs this is acceptable now**: views
here (Slice, and planned Reshape/Squeeze/Transpose/Expand) are cheap, layout-
only, and short-lived, and today there is no arena to shrink (one buffer per
value already lives the whole run regardless). The cost only becomes real once
the interval planner exists — at which point rule 2 (interval-granular pinning)
recovers it. Minor wart today: a statically-shaped value that becomes a view
gets a buffer allocated in `size_buffers` at run start and immediately freed at
1129-1131 (one wasted alloc/free); data-dependent views like Slice avoid it
(they stay unresolved, skipped by `size_buffers`).

**Open risks / holes found:** **None found.** Today's conservative pinning is
sound against use-after-free across every path examined (view-of-view flatten,
symbolic/dynamic reshape, control-flow subgraph capture, strided-unaware
consumers, cross-run reuse). The only failure mode would be a *future* kernel
that frees or donates a buffer other than the one it is producing, or a
`view_outputs` implementation that reports a stale `input_index` after a
resize — both are structurally prevented today (the resize/reproduce guards at
1124 and 1166, plus SSA ordering). Note the two guards are `debug_assert!`
(compiled out in release); they document invariants rather than enforce them at
runtime, so any future code that breaks SSA-topo ordering of view producers
would silently regress. Recommend upgrading them to hard `return Err(Internal)`
if/when an in-place or buffer-donation path is added.

#### Source: `sapper-review-concat.md`

### 2026-07-14: Concat direct-copy review
**By:** Sapper
**Verdict:** 🟡 SHIP-WITH-NOTES

**Offset math:** Correct. The contiguous destination formula is `((outer_idx * output_axis_len) + axis_prefix) * inner_bytes`; the strided formula is the same in elements with `axis_idx` and `inner_idx` added. Concrete 3-input 3D check for axis 1: A=[2,1,2], B=[2,2,2], C=[2,1,2], output=[2,4,2], `outer=2`, `inner_elems=2`, prefixes A/B/C=0/1/3. Destination element starts are outer 0: A=0, B=2, C=6; outer 1: A=8, B=10, C=14. Their slab lengths are 2/4/2 elements, filling [0,8) and [8,16) exactly without gaps or overlap. Axis 0 reduces to `outer=1` and sequential whole-input slabs; last-axis reduces to `inner_elems=1` and correctly interleaves each row by the output-axis stride.

**Dtype:** Correct for every fixed-width dtype supported by `elem_size`; copies use `esize` only, with no per-dtype branch. The u8 test validates 1-byte elements and the i64 test validates 8-byte elements. String and packed 4-bit types are rejected actionably rather than silently mishandled, consistent with the existing raw-byte helper contract.

**Strided inputs:** Correct. `input.is_contiguous()` gates slab memcpy, so a non-contiguous input cannot enter the contiguous path. Gather computes logical offsets from each view's element strides, including negative strides, while `TensorView::data_ptr()` first applies `byte_offset`; each element is copied directly to its final dense destination. The included transpose test exercises non-contiguous gather. Note: coverage does not explicitly combine nonzero `byte_offset` or negative strides with Concat, although the implementation uses the correct TensorView origin and signed strides.

**Race safety:** Single-threaded. Each `(input, outer_idx)` slab / logical element maps to a disjoint output interval, and no destination is written twice. `copy_nonoverlapping` relies on the executor's separate SSA output allocation, as documented by the kernel.

**Errors:** Axis-out-of-range and mismatched non-concat dimensions include WHAT/WHY/HOW, offending axis/input index, and shapes; validation occurs before writes, so the mismatch test confirms the output remains untouched. Empty inputs/output, scalar rank, dtype mismatch, invalid views, output layout/shape, and overflow also return descriptive errors rather than panicking. Nonblocking note: the rewrite no longer rejects more than one output view; it uses `outputs[0]` and ignores extras. The executor should always supply exactly one Concat output, but retaining exact arity validation would make the kernel boundary stricter.

**Tests/build:** Offline `cargo build -p onnx-runtime-ep-cpu` passed. Offline `cargo test -p onnx-runtime-ep-cpu --lib` passed: 196 passed, 0 failed, confirming Zhora's claim. Concat tests cover axis 0, middle axis, negative/last axis with three inputs, f32/u8/i64, a transposed non-contiguous input, axis bounds, and mismatched non-concat dimensions. Coverage gap is limited to explicit byte-offset/negative-stride Concat cases and extra-output arity.

# MLX EP end-to-end perf (via onnx-genai) + teardown memory-safety fixes

**By:** Coordinator (perf phase) · **Date:** 2026-07-13 · **Machine:** Apple M1 Max
**Model:** `models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe` · **Bin:** `profile_decode` (release, `--features bench-ort`)
**EP:** `ONNX_GENAI_EP=metal` + `ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_LIB=.../libonnxruntime_mlx_ep.dylib` (EP name `MLXExecutionProvider`)

## Warm perf (≥2 discard runs; medians)

| Metric | MLX EP | CPU EP | MLX vs CPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT / prefill, 26-tok prompt | 120 ms | 222 ms | **1.85× faster** |
| TTFT / prefill, 256-tok | 564 ms | 1504 ms | **2.67× faster** |
| TTFT / prefill, 512-tok | 1091 ms | 3019 ms | **2.77× faster** |
| Decode tok/s (65 new tok) | 116 tok/s | **189 tok/s** | **0.61× (MLX slower)** |

- **Prefill/TTFT is the MLX win** — 1.85–2.77×, scaling with prompt length (compute-bound GEMM). Confirms the EP as a TTFT accelerator on Apple Silicon.
- **Decode LOSES to the CPU int8 recipe on this 0.5B model** (116 vs 189). MLX decode is weight-bandwidth-bound + per-token GPU-launch/graph overhead; CPU's `accuracy_level=4` int8 SDOT path is extremely fast on a small model. Coherent output both paths.
- Profiler: `ort.session_run` ≈ 98.9% of per-token time (orchestration ~1%) — runtime is not the bottleneck; the kernel is.

## 🛑 Teardown use-after-free (FIXED) — memory safety
`profile_decode` with the metal EP segfaulted at process exit **10/10** (results always printed first; correctness unaffected). Three progressively-revealed UAFs, all from the plugin **factory being released before the InferenceSession**:
1. `plugin_ep::DataTransfer::~DataTransfer` → freed factory-shared DataTransfer singleton (no-op Release). **Fix:** ORT owns each instance; `new` in Create, `delete` in Release (mirrors the Allocator). *(onnxruntime-mlx f0fcc86)*
2. `Tensor::~Tensor` → `MetalContext::Free` on a destroyed context (raw pointer). **Fix:** `MetalContext` is a `shared_ptr` shared into `MetalAllocator`/`MetalEp`. *(onnxruntime-mlx f0fcc86)*
3. **Root cause:** `onnx-genai-engine::Engine` declared `_environment` BEFORE the session fields; Rust drops fields in declaration order, so the ORT Env (owns the plugin factory) dropped before the sessions. **Fix:** `_environment` is now the LAST field. *(onnx-genai)*
- Result: **0/10 teardown crashes.** Also restored `gemma4_assistant.rs`, which a prior docs commit (6d4d4d2) had accidentally deleted — the workspace hadn't compiled since.

## Next perf levers (ranked) — "怎么才能更加提升"
1. **bf16 end-to-end decode** (biggest bandwidth lever + fixes the ~token-14 fp32 drift). MLX already uses int4 weights; move activations/compute to bf16 to halve fp32 dequant bandwidth. *cheap-ish, high impact*
2. **MLX compiled-graph reuse across decode steps** — avoid the per-token graph rebuild + eval overhead (Phase-0 identified this as the batch-1 tax). *medium*
3. **Measure & eliminate mid-graph CPU-fallback round-trips** — ORT still assigns some shape ops to CPU ("Some nodes were not assigned to the preferred EP"); quantify node placement and pull hot ones onto MLX to cut boundary host-copies. *medium*
4. **Test on larger models (3B/7B)** — MLX decode is bandwidth-bound; the GPU wins bigger as compute/byte grows. On 0.5B, CPU int8 is unbeatable for decode. *validation, not code*

**Product story:** the MLX EP is a **prefill/TTFT accelerator** (1.85–2.77× on Apple Silicon, growing with prompt length); decode on small models stays on CPU's fast int8 path. Decode competitiveness should improve with bf16 + graph reuse + larger models.

### 2026-07-14: BF16 decode is end-to-end but slower on M1 Max
**By:** Copilot
**What:** Enable BF16 as a shared-buffer GQA KV/logits dtype in onnx-genai, add Mobius `mlx` BF16 GQA export capabilities, and allow BF16 GroupQueryAttention in onnxruntime-mlx. On Apple M1 Max, the BF16 model is coherent but measures 18.91 tok/s versus 69.47 fp32 and 103.35 Q4, so BF16 should not become the default on this hardware.
**Why:** The end-to-end path is correct and halves model/KV storage, but this generation of Apple GPU does not realize a BF16 decode-speed benefit; hardware-specific gating or FP16 evaluation is the next performance step.

### 2025 Deferred-todo investigation (GatherND, runtime Range, hybrid decode, Blocker #2)

**By:** Copilot (coding agent)

Worked through the five long-standing pending/blocked todos. Outcome:

- **GatherND** — IMPLEMENTED (commit e9c0056). ai.onnx batch_dims=0, compile-safe (static output
  shape; runtime index values via mlx_take). Bit-exact vs ORT CPU across 7 shapes incl negatives.
- **Runtime Reshape/Expand** — already done (shape-const int64 shape input; registered).
- **Runtime Range** — correctly STAYS deferred, now with concrete evidence: claiming runtime-bounded
  Range puts it in the compiled closure where its output feeds a downstream shape/axes reader (e.g.
  expanded RMSNormalization's ReduceMean axes), forcing a mid-compile eval that aborts mlx_compile
  (closure.cpp:104). Const-bounds Range stays claimed. Documented in code + README.
- **Hybrid decode verify (dc-verify)** — VERIFIED. Built a tiny Qwen3.5-style hybrid (1
  DeltaNet/LinearAttention layer + 1 full-attention layer) via Mobius (build_from_module,
  task="hybrid-text-generation"). Multi-step decode is bit-close to ORT CPU (max|Δlogits| 1.8e-7).
  Perf root-caused: the full-attention `Attention` layer was declined for dynamic Q dims → CPU
  fragmentation.
- **Blocker #2 (dc-attn-capture)** — PART 1 DONE (commit f4a8a03): the ai.onnx Attention rank-3 claim
  now accepts dynamic batch/seq dims (hidden stays static for the head split), so the full-attention
  layer is captured instead of declined. Hybrid per-token 2.80 → 1.45 ms; op 1084/0, backend 1607/0.
  PART 3 REMAINS deferred: a *shapeless growing-KV capture* for Attention so decode does not retrace
  per token. The capture machinery (detect_shared_kv / kv_alias / delta_copyout) is hardwired to
  com.microsoft::GroupQueryAttention (compiled.rs:134/181/538); Attention's KV/mask contract differs
  (additive mask + is_causal, no seqlens_k). This is the large byte-exact-core change a prior attempt
  reverted — deferred deliberately rather than risk the GQA decode core autonomously; a demonstrable
  win also needs a larger hybrid model than fits on this machine (tiny models are dispatch-bound).

**Net:** GatherND shipped; Attention dynamic-dims capture shipped; hybrid decode correctness verified;
Range deferral confirmed + documented; Blocker #2 part 3 scoped with concrete rationale.


<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/copilot-foundry-model-audit.md -->
### 2025 Foundry Local model perf audit (onnxruntime-mlx MLX EP)

**By:** Copilot (coding agent)

**What:** Ran the Foundry Local catalog's distinct architectures through the MLX EP
(`/tmp/fl/run.py`, decode S=1/P=128 + prefill S=128, MLX vs CPU, max|Δ|). Results:

| model | arch | prefill | decode | notes |
|-------|------|---------|--------|-------|
| Phi-3.5-mini | Phi3 GQA(9) | 5.29× | 1.19× | fully claimed (1 Cast bool→int64 on CPU, negligible) |
| Phi-4-mini | Phi4 long-ctx | **5.78×** | 1.10× | **FIXED** — was CPU-fallback (see below) |
| Mistral-7B | GQA(7) growing-KV | 11.89× | **3.30×** | already optimal; GQA left on CPU (claiming it regressed decode to 0.71×) |
| gpt-oss-20b | MoE | — | — | OOM on this machine; QMoE + 12-input sink-GQA unclaimed (see below) |

qwen2.5-{0.5b,1.5b,7b,14b,coder}/deepseek share the qwen2.5 arch (external-rotary GQA, already fixed).

**Fix shipped (commit 9a3eff2):** Phi-4-mini builds its long-context RoPE cos/sin cache with
`If(Greater(total_seq_len, 4096))`. The `If` claim accepted any bool condition; `if_op` reads the
condition host-side via `raw_host`, which only reads Initializer/CtxInput — the `Greater` output is a
runtime intermediate. The MLX partition claimed the If, failed at runtime ("RawHost on non-constant
input"), and ORT fell the WHOLE partition back to CPU (no offload). Now `if_claim` requires the
condition to be host-readable (`NodeView::input_is_host_readable`, via `ValueInfo_GetValueProducer`:
no producer = graph input/initializer/outer-scope). Data-dependent Ifs cleanly decline to CPU
control-flow while body ops still offload. Prefill 1.01× → 5.78×.

**Known-unclaimed (not fixed — deliberate):**
- **Mistral 7-input growing-KV GQA:** leaving it on CPU is FASTER (decode 3.30× vs 0.71× if claimed).
  The growing external KV (`past_key_values.*`) can't be shapelessly captured, so a claimed decode
  retraces per token and merges the big MatMulNBits islands into one eager subgraph. CPU GQA + MLX
  matmuls wins. (Requires blocker-#2 shapeless growing-KV capture to change.)
- **gpt-oss-20b MoE:** `QMoE` (24×, no handler) and a **12-input** sink-attention GQA (24×) are both
  large new features; the 20B model OOM-kills on this machine so neither can be validated locally.
  Deferred — document as "MoE models not yet MLX-accelerated".

**Why:** User asked to run all Foundry models through the EP, find unclaimed/inefficiency, and fix
for speed. The one real bug (Phi-4 full-CPU fallback) is fixed; the remaining gaps are either
intentionally-faster-on-CPU (Mistral) or large deferred features (MoE).
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/copilot-gguf-mmproj-vision.md -->
### 2026-07-19: GGUF vision/audio (Gemma4) lives in a separate `clip`-arch mmproj file
**By:** Copilot (CLI)
**What:** Supporting Gemma4 vision/audio *from GGUF* means reading the companion
`mmproj-*.gguf`, not the text GGUF. Verified against
`unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF/mmproj-F16.gguf` (160 MB): `general.architecture = clip`,
`clip.has_vision_encoder`/`clip.has_audio_encoder = True`, vision projector_type
`gemma4uv` (image_size 224, patch_size 16, embedding_length 3840), audio projector_type
`gemma4ua` (num_mel_bins 128, embedding_length 640). Tensor prefixes are `v.*` (patch_embd,
patch_norm.1/2/3, position_embd) and `mm.*` (input_projection, a.input_projection) — 11
tensors, block_count=0 for this file. Mobius `_tensor_mapping.py` handles none of these
prefixes (only text-backbone gemma4 tensors); `_config_mapping.py` maps only `gemma4→gemma4_text`.
**Why:** The user asked to support GGUF vision encoders "in passing." Concretely that is a new
clip/mmproj path (reader already parses arbitrary tensors/metadata; the gap is tensor-name
mapping `v.*`/`mm.*` → HF vision/audio encoder names + a `clip.*`-driven encoder config/builder).
It is SECONDARY to the critical path (Mobius composite metadata emission + onnx-genai VLM
composite runtime); the vision/audio encoder can also come from the HF checkpoint, which Mobius
already exports. Note block_count=0 in this mmproj suggests a shallow conv-stem+projector, so
verify the full vision tower coverage before committing to a GGUF-only vision path.
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/copilot-language-diffusion-llada.md -->
### 2026-07-19: Language diffusion — faithful LLaDA low-confidence remasking
**By:** Copilot
**What:** Upgraded the `masked_diffusion` scheduler (pipeline.rs) from raw max-logit confidence to the faithful LLaDA `generate` algorithm: the confidence that ranks masked positions for remasking is now the clean-softmax probability of the chosen token (`remasking="low_confidence"`), top-k selection is per-sequence, and a `temperature` knob applies Gumbel-max sampling (identity at 0). Added `temperature` + `block_length` to `SchedulerSpec`. `block_length` (semi-autoregressive) is parsed but bails as not-yet-supported. Added `scripts/masked_diffusion_parity.py` which validates onnx-genai exactly against the reference LLaDA `generate` (single block, cfg=0, temp=0) via a deterministic coupled ONNX LM, and proves `ceil(remaining/remaining_steps)` == LLaDA `get_num_transfer_tokens`. `run_diffusion` now writes i64 for integer outputs (token sequences).
**Why:** The prior scheduler ranked by raw logit, which diverges from LLaDA's softmax-probability confidence and would pick a different commit order. This makes language diffusion faithful to the published algorithm and independently validated (there is no diffusers-equivalent reference library for discrete diffusion). Next: semi-autoregressive blocks (ld-blocks), unsupervised CFG (ld-cfg), Mobius metadata (ld-mobius), and a real model (ld-realmodel).
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/copilot-native-comfyui-runner.md -->
### 2026-07-19: Native `run_comfyui` binary replaces the Python driver

**By:** Copilot

**What:** Added a native Rust binary `run_comfyui` (`crates/onnx-genai/src/bin/run_comfyui.rs`) that parses a ComfyUI API-format workflow (`onnx-genai-comfyui-config`), tokenizes prompt + negative prompt with the HuggingFace `tokenizers` crate (CLIP `tokenizer.json`, fixed pad/truncate 77, pad id 49407), runs the onnx-genai iterative diffusion pipeline, and saves PNG(s). Deleted `scripts/run_comfyui.py`. Added `PipelineEngine::diffusion_init_noise_sigma()` (public `Scheduler::init_noise_sigma`, default 1.0). The Mobius exporter (`checkpoint_export.py`) now emits a self-contained fast-format `tokenizer.json` (and `tokenizer_2.json` for SDXL) into the package root.

**Why:** The runner should consume an already-exported ONNX package with no Python and no re-export. Reusing the engine's scheduler for `init_noise_sigma` avoids duplicating sigma math. Emitting `tokenizer.json` at export time makes the package self-contained (the HF CLIP cache only carries vocab.json + merges.txt, which `tokenizers` cannot load). Verified bit-identical (max|Δ|=0) to the reference driver by tensor replay, and a coherent standalone render.
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/copilot-scheduler-scale-input.md -->
### 2026-07-13: Scheduler trait gains an optional `scale_input` hook
**By:** Copilot (coding agent)
**What:** Extended the public `Scheduler` trait (crates/onnx-genai-engine/src/pipeline.rs) with a
second, default-provided method:
`fn scale_input(&self, step, num_steps, sample: &Value) -> Result<Option<Value>>` (default `Ok(None)` = identity).
It transforms the loop-carried denoiser INPUT before the model runs. `run_iterative` now tracks the
raw (unscaled) loop sample separately from the scaled one: the raw sample drives `scheduler.step`, the
scaled sample is fed to the denoiser as a per-port override (composing with CFG overrides).
`run_denoiser_pass` now takes `overrides: &[(&str, &Value)]` and no longer returns `sample_in`.
Added the `euler` built-in scheduler (EulerDiscreteScheduler, epsilon) which uses this hook.
**Why:** Sigma-space schedulers (Euler and its relatives) must rescale the latent by
`1/sqrt(sigma^2+1)` before the denoiser — DDIM/masked-diffusion do not. Making input scaling a
default-None trait method keeps existing schedulers untouched (they don't implement it) while letting
user-supplied schedulers hook the input transform. Validated numerically against diffusers
(scripts/euler_parity.py). Anyone writing a custom `Scheduler` may now override `scale_input`; those
who don't get the previous behavior unchanged.
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/deckard-fp8-kv.md -->
### 2026-07-12: Use portable scaled E4M3FN and E5M2 for FP8 KV storage
**By:** Deckard
**What:** `onnx-genai-kv` supports FP8 E4M3FN (the default inference-oriented format) and E5M2. A software bit codec performs round-to-nearest, ties-to-even conversion, canonicalizes NaNs, and saturates infinities/overflow. Pages store compact FP8 bytes with independent scales per layer, K/V component, and KV head; metadata defaults, per-layer minimum precision, negative layer indices, and `sensitive_layers` select mixed precision. Exhaustive codec tests round-trip every finite FP8 encoding. Deterministic scaled cache vectors measured E4M3FN max absolute error 2.857143 at magnitude 200 (4.7619% max relative) and E5M2 max absolute error 0.7 at magnitude 10.3 (6.7961% max relative).
**Why:** Software conversion is portable across current CPU/GPU backends and does not require target-native FP8 instructions. Per-head scaling uses the available FP8 range while mixed compact buffers preserve the memory benefit when only sensitive layers remain at higher precision. Engine follow-up must replace the current hard-coded `KvDType::F32` bridge configuration with `PagedKvCache::new_with_metadata` (or an equivalent runtime-selected `KvQuantConfig`).
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/deckard-json-schema.md -->
### 2026-07-12: Generate inference metadata JSON Schema from Rust types
**By:** Deckard
**What:** `schemars` derives on `onnx-genai-metadata` are the source of truth for the canonical Draft 2020-12 `schema/inference_metadata.schema.json`; a generator binary and exact sync test keep the committed schema aligned.
**Why:** The runtime and Mobius share the Rust `InferenceMetadata` contract, so deriving the standard deliverable prevents a hand-maintained schema from drifting from accepted fields, aliases, defaults, enum vocabularies, and requiredness.
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/freysa-leak-test.md -->
### 2026-07-13: Guard Metal EP session buffer lifetime with device allocation telemetry
**By:** Freysa
**What:** Add a bounded Objective-C++ CTest that measures the shared Metal device's `currentAllocatedSize` after repeated Qwen Metal EP session destruction, plus a validation-layer runner for the E2E and leak tests.
**Why:** The EP is MRR, so replacing `-release` with assignment to `nil` silently leaks roughly one model's device weights per session. Direct Metal allocation telemetry catches that regression before unified memory exhaustion, while validation layers surface API misuse and GPU faults.


<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/harden-claims.md -->
# Decision: MLX EP — crash-safe claims, but handle zero-size tensors ON MLX

**Branch:** `fix/claim-hardening` (worktree `onnxruntime-mlx-harden`)
**Author:** Metal/MLX EP engineer
**Date:** 2026-07-13 (corrected pass)
**Priority:** memory-safety / stability **without** giving up MLX coverage

## Principle (corrected)

A claimed op **must never crash** — but crash-safety must be achieved by
**handling the degenerate case on the MLX path**, *not* by declining zero-size
inputs to the CPU EP. Empty / zero-size operands stay **claimed** and produce
the exact ONNX/numpy-reference output (shape, and values where defined) on MLX.
The only forms still declined to CPU are `float64` (a hardware limit — Apple
GPUs have no fp64) and absent-optional inputs handled via their defaults.

> This **supersedes** the earlier "reject any statically-empty operand → CPU"
> rule. Rejecting empties to CPU was crash-safe but wrong per the directive:
> those ops should run on MLX. The zero-size reject helpers were removed.

## What changed (onnx-tests conformance CRASH: 16 → 0, PASS 28 → 37)

Three crash classes; #2 is now fixed **in the handlers**, not the claim:

1. **Claim-time null-deref** (kept) — optional inputs ORT omits surface as a
   NULL `OrtValueInfo`; `GetName()`/`TensorInfo()` on them segfaults during
   `GetCapability`. Guarded for Clip, Slice, Split, Pad, Trilu, Reduce*, Conv
   bias, LayerNorm/SkipLayerNorm. An op with an absent optional stays **claimed**
   and uses the default.
2. **Zero-size / empty inputs** (now handled on MLX, `src/ep/ops/*.cc`):
   - *Construction-abort ops* — `mlx_max`/`mlx_min`/`mlx_logsumexp` `abort()` at
     op construction on an empty array. `ReduceMax`/`ReduceMin` route empties
     through `EmptyMinMaxReduce` (ONNX-reduced shape filled with the reduction
     identity via `mlx_full`); `LogSoftmax` emits `mlx_zeros_like`. Softmax /
     Sum / Prod / Mean / all elementwise compute empties natively.
   - *Empty-output CopyOut crash* — `mlx_matmul` / `mlx_pad` return an empty
     array with **no backing buffer**; the boundary `CopyOut` typed accessor
     segfaults. Handler re-materialises the empty result as a clean
     `mlx_zeros(shape, dtype)` (0 elements ⇒ value-irrelevant).
   - *Expand broadcast* — output dims computed with numpy bidirectional
     broadcast rules (size-1 dim takes the other operand's size, incl. `0`),
     not a naive `max`, so `[3,0]`↔`[3,1]` no longer aborts `mlx_broadcast_to`.
     **Expand now PASSES.**
3. **float64 on the Metal GPU** (kept → CPU) — MLX aborts materialising doubles
   on the Metal stream. **Unavoidable hardware limit**, not a policy choice;
   dropped `DOUBLE` from `IsMovableType` / `IsBoundaryValueType`. A future
   option is an MLX *CPU-device* route for fp64; out of scope here.

## Convention going forward

- Every claim predicate touching an optional input MUST gate it through
  `SlotPresent`/`ValueInfoPresent` before any ValueInfo method.
- **Do NOT reject zero-size operands in the claim.** Keep the claim permissive
  and handle the empty case in the handler: detect `mlx_array_size(x)==0` and
  `Bind` a correctly-shaped MLX array (`mlx_zeros`/`mlx_full`/broadcast) matching
  the ONNX output, routed through `ctx.Keep` (no raw new/delete).
- Only decline `float64` (Metal has no fp64).

## Verification

- Build green; ctest green (`mlx_op_tests`, `mlx_leak_test`, `mlx_e2e` — the
  "…Paris" coherence gate); `pytest tests/ops` **380 passed / 1 skipped**.
- Conformance (`MAX_EXAMPLES=25 SEED=0`): **CRASH 16 → 0**, PASS 28 → **37**,
  FAIL → 34. `PROFILE=1` confirms zero-size cases run **on MLX** (`ran_on_MLX=
  True`) for MatMul/Pad/Expand/Softmax/LogSoftmax/Where/ReduceMax/ReduceMin/
  ReduceSum, each matching the reference output shape/values.

## Not addressed (out of scope; documented in RESULTS.md)

- **`op`×`dtype` coverage gaps** (e.g. `uint16`/`int16` Relu/Min/Max/Where/Pad,
  integer `Mean`): ORT CPU *also* lacks a kernel (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), so neither
  backend can compute them — reproduces with non-empty inputs, so unrelated to
  zero-size. Optionally tighten these claims later (turns the init abort into a
  cleaner CPU decline; no pass/fail change).
- fp16 precision (Elu/Softplus/Mish/HardSwish), NaN propagation (Sign/PRelu),
  integer overflow (ReduceProd/ReduceL2/ReduceMean), Pow large-magnitude/fp64 —
  pure-correctness edges, left as known conformance-tolerance gaps.
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/leon-embed-api.md -->
### 2026-07-12: Expose pooled hidden-state embeddings from the engine
**By:** Leon
**What:** `Engine::embed(&mut self, input_ids: &[TokenId]) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<f32>>` performs mean pooling without normalization. `Engine::embed_with_options(&mut self, input_ids: &[TokenId], options: EmbeddingOptions) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<f32>>` selects `EmbeddingPooling::{Mean, LastToken}`, optional L2 normalization, and an optional explicit hidden-state output name. The engine auto-detects common hidden-state outputs, accepts fp32/fp16 tensors shaped per token, widens through `to_vec_f32_lossy`, and returns a capability error when no usable per-token hidden output exists.
**Why:** `/v1/embeddings` needs real model-derived fixed-width vectors without fabricating embeddings for logits-only models. Keeping pooling and normalization in the engine gives server callers a stable model-execution contract while allowing model-specific output selection when graphs expose multiple hidden layers.


<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/leon-fp8-fix.md -->
# Decision: fp8/int8 KV page-scaling redesign (per-token scales)

**Author:** Leon (Engine Dev — KV & buffers)
**Date:** 2026-07-12
**Supersedes numerics of:** `deckard-fp8-kv` (Chew REJECTED — Deckard locked out per reviewer protocol)
**Scope:** `crates/onnx-genai-kv/**` only. No metadata schema changes.

## Problem (Chew, BLOCKING)
Every `append_token_kv` on a quantized page called `page.dequantized(config)` over the
**whole page**, overwrote one token, then `store_from_f32` **recomputed a single per-head
scale from all tokens and re-encoded every token**. So each append requantized all
previously-stored tokens with a growing `max_abs`, and fp8 error **accumulated across page
fill** instead of being a one-time per-write cost. The old fp8/int8 tests used
`page_size = 1`, so a page never held more than one token and the bug was invisible.

## New design: per-token (per-(component, head, token)) scales
- **Scale granularity changed** from one scale per `(component, head)` (shared across the
  whole page) to one scale per `(component, head, token)`. Storage grew from
  `num_kv_heads` to `num_kv_heads * page_size` scales per quantized component, laid out
  `[head, token]` at `scale_offset + head * page_size + token`.
- **Append is now a single-token write.** The old dequantize-whole-page / requantize-whole-page
  path is deleted (`store_from_f32` and `dequantized` removed). `Page::write_head_token`
  computes the scale from **only the incoming token's `head_dim` values** and writes **only
  that token's bytes + its own scale**. Every other token slot (bytes and scale) is untouched.
- **Codec unchanged.** The E4M3FN/E5M2 bit codec (`fp8.rs`) is exactly as Chew approved.

### Why stored entries are never requantized
A token's quantized bytes are a pure function of that token's own values and its own frozen
scale, both written once at append time. Later appends address disjoint byte ranges and a
disjoint scale slot. Proven by test: an in-page token is **byte-identical** to the same token
quantized in isolation, regardless of how many later tokens fill the page.

## Multi-token-page error test (the test that would have caught this)
`fp8_full_page_never_requantizes_previously_stored_tokens` — `page_size = 16`, E4M3FN, fills a
full page with tokens whose magnitude spans six orders (token 0 carries Chew's `1.061`, later
tokens up to `2^21`). Asserts:
1. per-entry **relative error ≤ 7 %** across the whole page (E4M3 = 3 mantissa bits → ≤6.25%);
2. token 0's `1.061` is preserved (`|.-1.061| < 0.07`);
3. in-page token 0 bytes == isolated token 0 bytes (no requantization).

Numbers (measured against the real codec):
| max token magnitude | OLD whole-page scale → token0 `1.061` | error |
|---|---|---|
| 2^15 | 1.00000 | 5.7% |
| 2·10^5 | 0.87193 | 17.8% |
| 2^21 (test value) | **0.00000** | **100%** (collapses to zero) |
| — NEW per-token — | **1.06100** | **0.00%** |

`int8_full_page_error_is_bounded_and_stable` — `page_size = 8`, int8, same magnitude spread,
asserts per-entry relative error ≤ 1 % and byte-identical stored-token stability.

### Worst-case per-entry error over a full page (bounded, fill-independent)
Because the scale is per token, error is bounded **per write** and does **not** grow with page
occupancy:
- **E4M3FN:** token max maps to 448 (`0x7e`, exact); other in-token values ≤ ~2^-4 = **6.25%**
  relative (values <1/64 of the token max fall in the subnormal region — larger relative, but
  negligible absolute).
- **E5M2:** ≤ ~2^-3 = **12.5%** relative (2 mantissa bits), max 57344.
- **int8:** ≤ ~1/127 ≈ **0.8%** relative.

## quantization_axis handling
`KvComponentTolerance.quantization_axis` was silently ignored. Now validated in
`KvQuantConfig::from_metadata`: **per_token** (and unspecified) is the implemented axis and is
accepted; **per_channel** (and any unknown axis) is **rejected explicitly** with
`KvError::UnsupportedQuantizationAxis`. Rationale: a per-channel scale is derived across the
**token** axis, so appending a token would change the channel scale and force a rewrite of
every stored token — that directly violates the append-without-requantize invariant. Rejecting
is honest; silently downgrading to per-head-per-page was the source of the bug.
Test: `metadata_rejects_per_channel_quantization_axis`.

## int8 legacy `quant_scale` contract — break made explicit
The public `Page.quant_scale` field held only the *first* of many scales, so external callers
doing `q * page.quant_scale` decoded most entries wrong (and would be even more wrong with
per-token scales). It cannot represent a per-(head, token) scale set, so it is **removed**
(compile-time break, not a silent wrong value). Correct decode goes through `Page::value_at` /
`materialize_sequence`, which apply the right per-token scale. No workspace caller used the
field except the CoW copy, which now clones `quant_scales` wholesale.

## Files changed (no commit — coordinator commits)
- `crates/onnx-genai-kv/src/page_table.rs` — per-token scale layout; `value_at` per-token index;
  new `Page::write_head_token` + `quant_scale()` helper; removed `store_from_f32`/`dequantized`/
  `quant_scale` field; `validate_quant_axis`.
- `crates/onnx-genai-kv/src/paged_cache.rs` — single-token append path; CoW copy drops
  `quant_scale`; 3 new tests; updated the metadata-policy test axis to `per_token`.
- `crates/onnx-genai-kv/src/lib.rs` — `KvError::UnsupportedQuantizationAxis`.

## Validation
- `cargo test -p onnx-genai-kv` → **exit 0** (30 unit + 1 integration + 0 doc, all pass).
- `cargo clippy -p onnx-genai-kv --all-targets -- -D warnings` → **exit 0** (0 warnings).
<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/leon-metal-ep-wiring.md -->
### 2026-07-13: Wire the Metal plugin EP through ORT 1.27's plugin API
**By:** Leon
**What:** `ONNX_GENAI_EP=metal` selects a strict macOS arm64 `ExecutionProvider::Metal` path. The runtime validates the absolute `ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_LIB` path, registers it once per ORT environment as `MetalEP` with `RegisterExecutionProviderLibrary`, selects matching `OrtEpDevice` instances from `GetEpDevices`, and appends them with `SessionOptionsAppendExecutionProvider_V2`. Metal setup/session failures are returned instead of silently falling back to CPU. The sys build script reads the plugin's Mach-O dependency when the plugin env var is set and links/rpaths the host against that same ORT installation, preventing two ORT dylibs from loading into the process.
**Why:** ORT plugin EPs are environment-registered device providers rather than built-in string EPs. Strict selection makes Metal benchmarks trustworthy, and sharing the exact ORT dylib between host and plugin avoids crossing opaque ORT objects between two runtime copies.


<!-- merged from .squad/decisions/inbox/mariette-gqa-kernel.md -->
# Metal GroupQueryAttention kernel — whole-decoder fusion (27 → 1 subgraph, 67.9 → 98.6 tok/s)

**By:** Mariette (Metal/MPS Kernel Engineer)
**Date:** 2026-07-13
**Machine:** Apple M1 Max, macOS 25.x
**Repo:** `onnxruntime-mps` (Metal EP). Model: `onnx-genai/models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe/model.onnx` (fp32; num_heads=14, kv_num_heads=2, head=64, do_rotary=1).
**No commit — coordinator commits.**

## TL;DR

`com.microsoft.GroupQueryAttention` (24 nodes) now runs as a Metal kernel and is claimed in
GetCapability. This lets the **entire decoder fuse into a single subgraph**:

| metric | before (GQA on CPU) | after (Metal GQA) |
|---|---:|---:|
| fused subgraphs (GetCapability) | 27 | **1** |
| GPU command-buffer commits / token | ~27 | **1** |
| decode tok/s (64-tok) | 67.9 | **98.6** (+45%) |
| 8-token coherence gate | PASS | **PASS** |
| Metal-GQA vs CPU-GQA token stream (64 tok) | — | **byte-identical** |

CPU EP reference on this box: ~132–156 tok/s. llama.cpp Metal ~200. Remaining gap is *not* GQA
(see "Remaining gap").

## Kernel design (`src/kernels/gqa.metal`, two fp32 kernels, one encoder)

Semantics verified differentially against the ORT CPU-EP op (see Correctness). Grouped-KV,
RoPE, causal + sliding-window, share-buffer KV cache.

- **Pass 1 — `mps_gqa_write_kv_f32`** (grid `(present_seq, kv_num_heads, batch)`, tg = head threads):
  builds the present K/V cache. For each present position: copy past K/V (`pos < past`) or
  RoPE-and-append the new K (V un-roped) for `past ≤ pos < total`. Works whether present aliases
  past (true share-buffer, copy is identity) or is a separate growing buffer (strided copy of the
  `[0,past)` region using distinct past_seq/present_seq strides). Per-batch validity via the
  device `seqlens_k` (`total = seqlens_k[b]+1`, `past = total − S`).
- **Pass 2 — `mps_gqa_attention_f32`** (grid `(S, num_heads, batch)`, tg = T flash threads):
  flash-decoding / tiled attention with **online softmax** (running max `m`, denom `l`), fp32
  accumulation. Keys are split across `T` threads (threadgroup partials `qrot[HS]`, `m[T]`,
  `l[T]`, `acc[T*HS]`); `T` chosen on host from the pipeline max-threads and the threadgroup-memory
  budget (`(HS + 2T + T·HS)·4 ≤ device limit`, rounded to a multiple of 32). Grouped KV head =
  `h / (num_heads / kv_num_heads)`. Causal keys `[lo, posn]` inclusive; sliding window
  `lo = max(0, posn − local_window + 1)` when `local_window_size ≥ 0`, else `lo = 0`.
- RoPE matches the existing `rope.metal` convention (non-interleaved half-split *and* interleaved);
  cos/sin cache is `[max_seq, rotary_dim/2]`, indexed by absolute position `past + i`.
- Both passes encode into **one serial compute encoder** (the shared batch encoder in a fused
  subgraph, else an own command buffer). An explicit `memoryBarrierWithScope:MTLBarrierScopeBuffers`
  separates Pass 1 (writes present) from Pass 2 (reads present) — per Nabil's guidance for
  multi-dispatch kernels sharing the single batch buffer.

## Wiring (`src/ep/ep.cc`, `ep.h`, `metal_context.{h,mm}`, `CMakeLists.txt`)

- `MarietteClaimable`: claims the 9-input separate-QKV fp32 GQA layout
  (q,k,v,past_k,past_v,seqlens_k,total_seq,cos,sin), `num_heads % kv_num_heads == 0`, rejecting
  smooth_softmax / softcap / qk_output variants.
- `MarietteKernel::ComputeIO` derives `GroupQueryAttentionParams` (scale, rotary_dim from
  `cos.shape[-1]*2`, `past_seq = past_k.shape[2]`, `present_seq = past_seq + S`) and dispatches
  `MetalContext::GroupQueryAttention`, which resolves every operand to a device buffer
  (LookupBuffer for device-resident tensors, else a wrapped host temp) and encodes the two passes.

## Two bugs found & fixed while landing this

1. **Schema-default attributes made the claim silently fail.** ORT materializes op schema defaults;
   `GetAttributeByName` returns *absent* optional INT attrs as type INT with the default — for this
   node `smooth_softmax = -1`, `local_window_size = -1`. The original `smooth_softmax != 0` guard
   therefore rejected **every** GQA node (claimed 366/393, 27 subgraphs, unchanged). Fixed to test
   the *enabled* sentinel (`== 1`) and hardened `IntAttribute`/`FloatAttribute` to validate
   `GetType()` before reading. (Repository memory stored.)
2. **Fused-path garbage from a host read of a device tensor.** `seqlens_k` / `total_sequence_length`
   are `Cast` outputs, and `Cast` is Metal-claimed — so in the fused subgraph they are
   **device-resident**, and the host dispatch reading `seqlens_k[b]` to size the write grid got a
   stale host shadow → whole-decoder output was garbage from token 0. Fixed by sizing the write grid
   and rotary-cache wrap from `present_seq` (shape-derived) and letting the **kernel** read
   `seqlens_k` on-device for per-batch validity. After the fix the fused stream equals the
   non-fused stream exactly. (Repository memory stored.)

## Correctness (GQA-specific, verified FIRST)

- **C++ CPU-reference** (`tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc`, `TestGroupQueryAttention`, tol 2e-3):
  8 cases — decode, decode-norope, decode-batch, prefill, prefill-interleaved, chunked, decode-SWA,
  prefill-SWA. **PASS.**
- **Differential vs ORT CPU-EP through the EP** (`tests/kernels/ort_reference_test.py`, rtol/atol 2e-3):
  13 cases including single-node decode/prefill/chunked/SWA/batch **and** multi-node fused
  (`Add → GQA → Add`, so GQA consumes/produces device-resident intermediates) at both toy dims and
  the real head=64/num_heads=14 geometry. **PASS.**
- **E2E** (`tests/e2e/mps_e2e`, growing KV cache): Metal-GQA token stream is **byte-identical to the
  CPU-GQA baseline** for all 64 tokens (verified by diffing the two runs). i.e. swapping CPU GQA for
  Metal GQA changes *nothing* in the output — the kernel is numerically faithful.
- ctest: `mps_kernel_tests`, `mps_mariette_tests`, `mps_ort_reference_tests` → **3/3 PASS**.

## Remaining gap (NOT GQA — pre-existing, out of scope)

The strict E2E coherence gate (full stream == pure CPU) still diverges at ~token 14. This is the
**known pre-existing fp32 reduction-order drift** flagged in `nabil-batched-dispatch.md`
("8-token coherence is the bar … ≥~14 tokens diverges … not dispatch"), rooted in `MatMulNBits`
(int8 `accuracy_level=4` on CPU vs fp32 dequant on Metal — see `sebastian-accuracy-level-debug.md`).
Proof it is not GQA: with GQA forced back to CPU the baseline diverges at the **same** token 14, and
Metal-GQA reproduces the CPU-GQA stream exactly. The **8-token gate PASSES**. Closing the pure-CPU
gap is a `MatMulNBits`-precision task (coordinate with Coco/Sebastian), independent of this kernel.

Perf headroom for a later pass: Pass-2 currently keeps `acc[T*HS]` in threadgroup memory; a
register-tiled variant + fp16 K/V loads should narrow the gap to llama.cpp Metal (~200).

## Files changed (coordinator to commit — I did NOT commit)
- `src/kernels/gqa.metal` — **new**: `mps_gqa_write_kv_f32`, `mps_gqa_attention_f32`, `gqa_rope_value`.
- `src/ep/metal_context.{h,mm}` — `GroupQueryAttentionParams` + `MetalContext::GroupQueryAttention`
  (two-pass single-encoder dispatch; device/host operand resolution; T selection; inter-pass barrier).
- `src/ep/ep.{h,cc}` — GQA claim in `MarietteClaimable`; attr parse + `ComputeIO` branch in
  `MarietteKernel`; `IntAttribute`/`FloatAttribute` type-guarded against schema-default phantoms.
- `tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc` — `GqaReference` + 8 CPU-ref cases.
- `tests/kernels/ort_reference_test.py` — 13 GQA differential cases (single-node + fused, head=16/64).
- `CMakeLists.txt` — add `src/kernels/gqa.metal` to the Metal kernel list.

## Reproduce
```bash
cd onnxruntime-mps/build && cmake . && cmake --build . -j8
ORTLIB=<onnx-genai>/target/release/build/onnx-genai-ort-sys-*/out/ort-prebuilt/lib
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ctest --output-on-failure
# E2E (coherence + tok/s + subgraph/commit counts):
ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_PROFILE=1 DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ./mps_e2e \
  <onnx-genai>/models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe/model.onnx \
  "$PWD/libonnxruntime_mps_ep.dylib" ../tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 8   # gate PASS at 8
```

# Decision: Metal decode hot-path kernels (MatMulNBits, RMSNorm, SkipSimplifiedLayerNorm, Softmax)

**Author:** Mariette (Metal/MPS Kernel Engineer)
**Date:** 2026-07-13
**Repo:** onnxruntime-mps
**Status:** Implemented, correctness-proven (E2E coherent + per-kernel vs CPU). Perf: see caveat.

## Scope

Implemented the compute-heavy decode kernels for the Metal EP, registered via Nabil's
compile-based dispatch and kept merge-isolated from Coco's parallel work (elementwise/gather/rope)
by mirroring Coco's separation pattern: a dedicated `MarietteKernel` struct + `mariette_kernels_`
map + `MarietteClaimable()` + `MarietteNodeComputeInfo`, added additively alongside (never
replacing) the Add/Coco registrations.

Kernels (own `.metal` files, loaded into the runtime-compiled library via CMake
`ORT_MPS_METAL_KERNEL_FILES` → `metal_kernels.inc`):

- **MatMulNBits** (`com.microsoft`, 169 nodes) — THE decode bottleneck.
- **SkipSimplifiedLayerNormalization** (`com.microsoft`, 48 nodes).
- **RMSNormalization** (`ai.onnx`, 1 node).
- **Softmax** (`ai.onnx`, 0 in this graph — unit-tested only).

## MatMulNBits design

int4 block-quantized weights, `bits=4`, `block_size=32`, 3 inputs (no zero_points → symmetric
default zp=8). Packing (ORT contrib, verified by per-kernel test + E2E coherence): B is
`[N, nblocks, 16]` uint8; within a 32-element block byte = k/2, **low nibble = even k**, high
nibble = odd k; `w[n][k] = (q - 8) * scale[n][block]`; `Y = A · dequant(B)^T` (+ optional bias).

- **Decode GEMV (M=1, memory-bound — the important case):** one 32-lane simdgroup per output
  column n; grid.x = N*32, grid.y = M, threadgroup = 256. Lane L owns within-block index L, sweeps
  all `nblocks` blocks reading 16 packed bytes + 32 activations coalesced, dequantizes, accumulates
  in fp32, then `simd_sum` reduces the 32 partials to Y[m,n]. All graph N are multiples of 8 so
  N*32 tiles the 256-wide threadgroup exactly and simdgroups stay full.
- **Prefill GEMM (M>1):** handled by the same kernel looping over M rows (grid.y = M). Correct;
  a tiled `simdgroup_matrix` GEMM is a future perf upgrade for large-M prefill.
- **Accuracy:** currently fp32 accumulation (matches the fp32 cpu-recipe graph and passes
  correctness). The `accuracy_level=4` int8-dynamic-quant + int8 dot-product fast path
  (llama.cpp `mul_mv_q`-style) is the next perf step; deferred to keep correctness first.

**Key perf lever — device-resident weights:** the constant B (uint8) + scales (fp32) are copied
into `MetalContext::Alloc`'d device buffers **once** on the first `Compute` and reused every decode
step (cached in the `MarietteKernel` object; freed in its dtor). Because Alloc'd pointers are
tracked in the context's buffer table, `LookupBuffer` resolves them zero-copy. This avoids
re-uploading ~350MB of weights per token. No changes to Coco's/Nabil's `Impl` struct.

## Norm kernels

- **RMSNormalization:** one threadgroup per row, `simd_sum` + threadgroup scratch reduction of
  sum(x²); `y = x / sqrt(mean(x²)+eps) * gamma`, fp32.
- **SkipSimplifiedLayerNormalization:** residual = input + skip (written to the last output when
  ORT keeps it — the fusion drops the unused mean/inv_std_var outputs, so we write out[0] =
  normalized always and out[count-1] = residual when output count > 1), then RMS-normalize.

## Correctness

- **Per-kernel** (`tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc`, target `mps_mariette_tests`): MatMulNBits
  (M=1 GEMV and M=3 GEMM), RMSNorm, SkipLN (normalized + residual), Softmax all match a scalar CPU
  reference. Tolerances: 1e-3 (matmul/norm, fp32 GPU reduction order), 1e-5 (softmax). **PASS.**
- **E2E** (`mps_e2e`, Qwen2.5-0.5B cpu-recipe, greedy): MetalEP token stream ==
  CPU token stream = `785 6722 315 9625 374 12095 13 151645` ("... is Paris."). **COHERENCE PASS.**
  With Coco's kernels also claimed, **366 / 393 nodes run on Metal** (72 Add + 169 MatMulNBits +
  48 SkipLN + 1 RMS + Coco's elementwise/gather/rope; remaining 27 fall back to CPU).

## Perf caveat (important, needs coordination)

Decode with the full graph on Metal is currently **~11.8 tok/s vs ~166 tok/s CPU** — a *loss*, not
a win, despite correct kernels. Root cause is **architectural, not per-kernel**: the shared dispatch
helpers (`Dispatch` in Coco's path, `RunPass` in mine) each do a full `commit` +
`waitUntilCompleted` + host memcpy copy-back **per node**. At 366 nodes/token that is ~366 GPU
round-trips + host copies per token, which serializes everything and dwarfs the actual compute.

The MatMulNBits kernel itself is correct and the weights are device-resident; the win it should
deliver is masked by per-node synchronization. **To realize Metal decode speedup we need a
framework change (shared, coordinate with Nabil + Coco):** batch a token's dispatches into one
command buffer with a single `waitUntilCompleted`, and keep intermediate tensors device-resident
(skip copy-back when an output feeds another Metal node) instead of round-tripping to host between
every op. That is the highest-leverage next step. After that, adding the int8 `accuracy_level=4`
fast path to MatMulNBits is the second lever to approach llama.cpp Metal.

## Files

Created: `src/kernels/matmulnbits.metal`, `src/kernels/norm.metal`, `src/kernels/softmax.metal`,
`tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc`.
Modified (all additive, merge-safe): `src/ep/ep.h`, `src/ep/ep.cc`, `src/ep/metal_context.h`,
`src/ep/metal_context.mm`, `CMakeLists.txt`.

## Build / test / run

```
cmake -S . -B build -G "Unix Makefiles" && cmake --build build -j8
./build/mps_mariette_tests            # per-kernel vs CPU reference
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=<ort-prebuilt>/lib ./build/mps_e2e \
  <qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe>/model.onnx $PWD/build/libonnxruntime_mps_ep.dylib \
  tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 8       # E2E coherence + tok/s
```

Note: Metal helper functions share one runtime-compiled program source, so helper names must be
globally unique across all `.metal` files (hit a `tg_reduce_sum` redefinition between norm.metal
and softmax.metal → renamed to `mps_norm_reduce_sum` / `mps_softmax_reduce_{sum,max}`).

# MatMulNBits decode GEMV — vectorized uint4 weight loads make fp32 the fast path (~106 → ~133 tok/s, +27%)

**By:** Mariette (Metal/MPS Kernel Engineer)
**Date:** 2026-07-13
**Machine:** Apple M1 Max, macOS 25.x (~400 GB/s theoretical UMA bandwidth)
**Repo:** `onnxruntime-mps` (Metal EP). Model: `onnx-genai/models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe/model.onnx`
(fp32 graph, 169 MatMulNBits, whole decoder = 1 fused subgraph = 1 commit/token).
**No commit — coordinator commits.**

## TL;DR

Decode is weight-bandwidth-bound (`mariette-matmulnbits-int8`): each token streams the full packed
int4 weight set once. The previous default kernel read those weights **one byte at a time** (with two
adjacent simd lanes hitting the *same* byte) — narrow 8-bit loads, only 16 weight-bytes moved per
simdgroup per loop step, so it never approached achievable memory throughput. Rewriting the load path
to **wide, fully-coalesced `uint4` (128-bit) transactions** — each lane owns a whole 32-element block
and the 32 lanes of a simdgroup read 32 consecutive blocks = **512 contiguous bytes** per step — lifts
steady decode from **~106 → ~133 tok/s (+~27%)**, with best runs momentarily matching the CPU EP
(~156). This is now the **default**. fp16-math on top gave **no** further gain (confirming the kernel
is bandwidth-bound, not ALU-bound) and adds a small quant error, so it stays opt-in.

| Metal MatMulNBits path (64-tok decode, steady; M1 Max) | decode tok/s | 8-tok gate |
|---|---:|:--:|
| scalar byte-load (`mps_matmulnbits_f32`, prior default) | ~106 | PASS |
| **uint4 wide-load fp32 (`mps_matmulnbits_f32_v`, NEW default)** | **~132–135 (peak ~156)** | **PASS** |
| uint4 wide-load fp16-math (`mps_matmulnbits_f16_v`, opt-in) | ~133 (no gain) | PASS |
| — CPU EP reference (same box) | ~153–159 | — |
| — llama.cpp Metal (reference) | ~200 | — |

Cold-start first run is a warmup outlier (~78 tok/s) and excluded from the steady median.

## The bandwidth fix (`src/kernels/matmulnbits.metal`)

New `mps_matmulnbits_f32_v` (dispatch identical to the old kernel: one 32-lane simdgroup per output
column `n`, grid = N*32 × M, 256-wide threadgroup = 8 columns):

- **Wide coalesced weight loads.** `B` is column-major `[nblocks][16 bytes]`, 16-byte aligned per
  column. Each lane loads a whole block's 16 packed bytes as a single **`uint4`** and strides
  `for (b = lane; b < nblocks; b += 32)`, so consecutive lanes always read consecutive blocks →
  the simdgroup issues one 512-byte contiguous burst per step (llama.cpp `kernel_mul_mv_*` layout),
  no redundant loads, no byte-granularity accesses.
- Activations read as **`float4`** (128-bit, aligned since `block_size==32` ⇒ K multiple of 4).
  Nibbles are unpacked into `float4`s and reduced with `dot()`; one **`simd_sum`** at the very end
  (each lane summed its complete blocks) — no per-block reduction.
- **fp32 accumulate** to hold the ORT CPU tolerance on long-K reductions.

`mps_matmulnbits_f16_v` is identical but converts the activation to `half` and multiplies in fp16
(fp32 per-block promote for the cross-block reduction). Weight bytes are byte-identical (the dominant
traffic is unchanged), so it only touches the ALU — and on this bandwidth-bound kernel that buys
nothing. Kept behind a flag for any future ALU-bound / lower-weight-byte regime.

The scalar `mps_matmulnbits_f32` (byte loads) is retained unchanged as the **correctness reference**.

## Occupancy / threadgroup sweep

Swept threads-per-threadgroup ∈ {64,128,256,512} (= 2/4/8/16 output columns per group) via
`ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_TG`. 256 and 512 were best and statistically tied (peaks ~156); 64 was
noisier with a low tail. **Kept 256** (8 columns/group) as the tuned default — the register/occupancy
sweet spot and consistent with the other Mariette kernels. Env knob left in place (defaults to 256)
for future tuning.

## Wiring (`src/ep/metal_context.{h,mm}`, `src/ep/ep.cc`)

`MetalContext::MatMulNBitsF32` gained a defaulted `MatMulNBitsVariant {Auto,Scalar,VectorF32,VectorF16}`
argument. `Auto` (production) = **VectorF32** unless overridden by env:
`ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_SCALAR=1` (reference), `…_FP16=1` (fp16 math),
`…_TG=<mult-of-32>` (threadgroup width). `ep.cc` is unchanged in behavior — the same call now hits the
vectorized kernel by default; constant weights remain device-resident (copied once). The `int8` path
(`ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_INT8`) is orthogonal and unchanged.

## Correctness (verified FIRST)

- **Per-kernel** (`tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc`, `TestMatMulNBits`, target
  `mps_mariette_tests`): all 3 variants at M∈{1,2,3} and **K∈{64, 1088}** — K=1088 = 34 blocks
  exercises the `b += 32` block-stride wrap and the ragged tail (>1 simdgroup of blocks, not a
  multiple of 32). vs the fp32 CPU reference: scalar & **VectorF32 exact within 1e-3**;
  **VectorF16 worst abs-err = 0.0031** (K=1088), bounded at 5e-2 (fp16-aware). 
- **ctest**: `mps_kernel_tests`, `mps_mariette_tests`, `mps_ort_reference_tests` → **3/3 PASS**
  (ort-reference differential still exact under the new default).
- **E2E** (`mps_e2e`, Qwen2.5-0.5B cpu-recipe, greedy): **8-token COHERENCE GATE PASS** for both the
  default (vec-fp32) and the fp16 opt-in — stream `785 6722 315 9625 374 12095 13 151645`
  == CPU ("The capital of France is Paris."). Fluent + correct. (The known pre-existing ~token-14
  fp32 reduction-order drift beyond 8 tokens is unchanged and out of scope —
  `mariette-gqa-kernel.md`, `nabil-batched-dispatch.md`.)

## Bandwidth estimate

Effective weight bandwidth ≈ decode tok/s × ~350 MB/token (whole-token wall clock, so a *lower bound*
on the kernel's true throughput since a token also spends time in GQA/norms/softmax/rope + the
per-token commit/wait):
- scalar prior default: 106 × 350 MB ≈ **37 GB/s** (~9% of 400 GB/s theoretical)
- **new vec-fp32 default: 133 × 350 MB ≈ 46–47 GB/s** (~12% of theoretical); peaks (~156) ≈ 55 GB/s

The +27% tok/s tracks the +27% effective bandwidth — i.e. the win is purely moving the weight bytes
more efficiently, exactly as predicted. The whole-token figure sits well under 400 GB/s because
weight streaming is only a fraction of per-token wall time; the MatMulNBits kernel itself sustains
materially higher, and the remaining headroom is non-kernel overhead.

## Remaining gap to CPU (~153) / llama.cpp Metal (~200)

Now at **~87% of CPU** and **~66% of llama.cpp Metal** (was ~69% / ~53%). What's left is *not* the
weight-load path:
- **per-token `waitUntilCompleted`** on the single fused subgraph — overlap encode/execute across the
  token boundary (double-buffer command buffers) to hide submit/sync latency;
- **non-MatMulNBits per-token time** (GQA, norms, softmax, rope, elementwise) now a larger relative
  share — profile with `ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_PROFILE` to find the next dominant node;
- possible further MatMulNBits micro-opt: 2-columns-per-lane to reuse each loaded activation across
  outputs, or `simdgroup_matrix` tiling for large-M prefill (separate from decode).
- fp16 **activations end-to-end** (graph dtype) would finally cut activation *device* traffic — but
  activation is KB-scale and L2-resident, so the payoff is small vs the weight stream.

## Files changed (coordinator to commit — I did NOT commit)
- `src/kernels/matmulnbits.metal` — **new** `mps_matmulnbits_f32_v` (uint4 wide-load, fp32) and
  `mps_matmulnbits_f16_v` (uint4 wide-load, fp16 math); scalar `mps_matmulnbits_f32` unchanged.
- `src/ep/metal_context.mm` — register both pipelines; `MatMulNBitsF32` variant selector + env
  overrides (`…_SCALAR`, `…_FP16`, `…_TG`); default = VectorF32.
- `src/ep/metal_context.h` — `MatMulNBitsVariant` enum + defaulted `variant` param + doc.
- `tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc` — `TestMatMulNBits` covers all 3 variants at K∈{64,1088}
  (block-stride + tail) and quantifies the fp16 error.

## Reproduce
```bash
cd onnxruntime-mps && cmake --build build -j8
ORTLIB=$(dirname $(ls <onnx-genai>/target/release/build/onnx-genai-ort-sys-*/out/ort-prebuilt/lib/libonnxruntime.dylib|head -1))
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure          # 3/3 PASS
MODEL=<onnx-genai>/models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe/model.onnx
EP=$PWD/build/libonnxruntime_mps_ep.dylib
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ./build/mps_e2e "$MODEL" "$EP" tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 8   # gate PASS
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ./build/mps_e2e "$MODEL" "$EP" tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 64  # tok/s
# A/B: force scalar reference, fp16 math, or a threadgroup width
ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_SCALAR=1 …   # prior byte-load kernel (~106)
ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_FP16=1   …   # fp16 math (~133, +small err)
ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_TG=512   …   # occupancy sweep
```

# MatMulNBits int8 dot-product fast path (Metal) — implemented & correct, but decode GEMV is weight-bandwidth-bound so fp32 stays default

**By:** Mariette (Metal/MPS Kernel Engineer)
**Date:** 2026-07-13
**Machine:** Apple M1 Max, macOS 25.x
**Repo:** `onnxruntime-mps` (Metal EP). Model: `onnx-genai/models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe/model.onnx` (fp32, 169 MatMulNBits).
**No commit — coordinator commits.**

## TL;DR

Added the int8 dynamic-quant fast path (accuracy_level=4 scheme, llama.cpp `mul_mv_q`-style) to the
Metal `MatMulNBits` kernel. It is **numerically faithful** (GPU int8 == scalar CPU int8 reference
exactly; worst-case error vs fp32 quantified below) and **coherent E2E** (8-token gate PASS). But on
the Apple GPU it is **~20% slower** than the existing fp32 dequant path for decode, because **decode
GEMV (M=1) is weight-bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound**. Both paths read the identical 4-bit packed
weight bytes (~350 MB, the dominant traffic); int8 only adds activation-quant + threadgroup-memory
occupancy overhead without cutting the bottleneck. This is the **opposite** of CPU, where
`accuracy_level=4` won 2.3× precisely because the ARM path was **SDOT-compute-bound**
(`sebastian-accuracy-level-debug.md`).

**Decision: keep fp32 as the default Metal decode path; ship the int8 kernel behind an opt-in
(`ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_INT8=1`), correctness-proven, for compute-bound / large-M or future
lower-bandwidth-weight regimes.**

| Metal MatMulNBits path (64-tok decode, steady) | decode tok/s | 8-tok gate |
|---|---:|:--:|
| **fp32 dequant (default)** | **~101–104** | **PASS** |
| int8 dynamic-quant (`…_INT8=1`) | ~80–85 | PASS |
| — CPU EP reference (same box) | ~150–160 | — |
| — llama.cpp Metal (reference) | ~200 | — |

Baseline going into this task was 98.6 (GQA decision, 64-tok); fp32 default measures ~101–104 here
(warmup/measurement noise) — i.e. **unchanged/slightly better**, no regression.

## int8 GEMV design (`src/kernels/matmulnbits.metal` → `mps_matmulnbits_i8`)

Single **fused** kernel (no separate quantize pass, no device scratch, no cross-pass barrier):

- Dispatch = same as fp32: one 32-lane simdgroup per output column `n`; grid.x = N*32, grid.y = M,
  threadgroup = 256 (⇒ **8 columns per threadgroup, all sharing one activation row** for M=1 decode).
- **Phase A (once per threadgroup):** the 8 simdgroups cooperatively dynamically-quantize the shared
  activation row to int8 into **threadgroup memory** — per K-block (block_size=32) symmetric absmax
  scale `a_scale = absmax/127`, `qa = clamp(round(a/ a_scale), -127, 127)`. `simd_max(|a|)` gives the
  block absmax; blocks are striped across the 8 simdgroups. `threadgroup_barrier` then publishes it.
  Quantizing once per 8 columns (vs once per column) is the amortization llama.cpp uses.
- **Phase B:** each simdgroup sweeps its column's blocks: unpack int4 weight → signed `(q-8)` in
  [-8,7], `prod = int(qa[k]) * wq`, **int32** `simd_sum(prod)` per block, then
  `acc += float(block_dot) * (a_scale[b] * w_scale[b])`; fp32 across blocks. Lane 0 writes Y (+bias).
- Handles M>1 (prefill) with the same kernel (grid.y = M). Not a tiled `simdgroup_matrix` GEMM — the
  large-M prefill tiling remains future work (as before).
- fp32 reference/fallback path `mps_matmulnbits_f32` kept unchanged (now the default).

Wiring (`src/ep/metal_context.{h,mm}`, `src/ep/ep.cc`): new `MetalContext::MatMulNBitsI8` encodes the
one fused dispatch (threadgroup-memory lengths for `tg_qa[K]` + `tg_ascale[nblocks]`), batch-aware
like the other kernels; `MarietteKernel::ComputeIO` selects int8 only when
`ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_INT8` is set, else fp32. Constant weights stay device-resident (unchanged).

## Why int8 doesn't win on the GPU (the measured finding)

Decode is **M=1 GEMV**: for each of 169 nodes the kernel streams the full 4-bit weight matrix and
does a tiny amount of math per weight. It is **memory-bandwidth-bound on the weights**, which are
**byte-identical** between fp32 and int8 (same packed uint8 `[N,nblocks,16]`). int8 therefore:
- does **not** reduce the dominant memory traffic (weights), and the activation is KB-scale (irrelevant);
- **adds** work: a `simd_max` reduction + quantize per block, plus threadgroup memory that lowers GPU
  occupancy (the head's K=896 ⇒ ~1 KB threadgroup/block, fewer resident threadgroups than the
  zero-threadgroup-memory fp32 kernel).

So int8's CPU win (SDOT throughput on a compute-bound kernel) does not transfer to this GPU regime.
Confirmed by 3× repeated A/B: int8 80–85 vs fp32 101–104 tok/s.

## Correctness (verified FIRST — precision-sensitive)

- **Per-kernel** (`tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc`, `TestMatMulNBitsInt8`, target
  `mps_mariette_tests`): M=1 and M=4, N=16, K=256. Two references:
  - vs a scalar **CPU int8** reference applying the identical per-block absmax quant → **exact match**
    (`worst |GPU-int8 − CPU-int8| = 0`). Proves the kernel implements accuracy_level=4 math faithfully.
  - vs the **fp32** dequant reference (the intrinsic quantization error): **worst 3.72% relative**
    (on |ref|≥0.1) / **0.017 absolute**. Gate = combined atol+rtol (`0.05 + 0.05·|ref|`); pure
    relative error is meaningless on near-zero cancellation outputs. **PASS.**
- **ctest**: `mps_kernel_tests`, `mps_mariette_tests`, `mps_ort_reference_tests` → **3/3 PASS** (default
  fp32; ort-reference differential still exact).
- **E2E** (`mps_e2e`, Qwen2.5-0.5B cpu-recipe, greedy, whole decoder = 1 fused subgraph, 1 commit/token):
  8-token stream == CPU = `785 6722 315 9625 374 12095 13 151645` ("... is Paris.") for **both** default
  fp32 **and** `…_INT8=1`. **8-token COHERENCE GATE PASS** both ways. (The known pre-existing ~token-14
  fp32 reduction-order drift is unchanged and out of scope — see `mariette-gqa-kernel.md`,
  `nabil-batched-dispatch.md`.)

## Remaining gap to CPU (~150–160) / llama.cpp Metal (~200)

Not MatMulNBits arithmetic. The decode is weight-bandwidth-bound and fp32 already sits near that bound
(~103 tok/s). To close on llama.cpp the levers are memory/dispatch, not int8 activation quant:
- **fp16 activations + fp16 accumulation** (halve activation traffic, native M-series fp16 throughput);
- **overlap encode/execute** across the 1 subgraph boundary (remove the per-token `waitUntilCompleted`);
- weight-read micro-opt (vectorized `uint4` loads of the packed bytes; better cache/coalescing);
- large-M prefill tiled `simdgroup_matrix` GEMM (separate from decode).
int8 would only help if a future weight format reduced weight bytes or a genuinely compute-bound
regime appeared (large-M GEMM) — the kernel is ready for that behind the flag.

## Files changed (coordinator to commit — I did NOT commit)
- `src/kernels/matmulnbits.metal` — **new** fused `mps_matmulnbits_i8` (threadgroup-cooperative int8
  quant + int32 dot); `mps_matmulnbits_f32` unchanged.
- `src/ep/metal_context.{h,mm}` — `MatMulNBitsI8` (single fused dispatch, threadgroup memory);
  register `mps_matmulnbits_i8` pipeline.
- `src/ep/ep.cc` — `MarietteKernel::ComputeIO` selects fp32 (default) vs int8 via
  `ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_INT8`.
- `tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc` — `TestMatMulNBitsInt8` (vs CPU-int8 exact + vs fp32 error
  quantification).

## Reproduce
```bash
cd onnxruntime-mps && cmake --build build -j8
ORTLIB=<onnx-genai>/target/release/build/onnx-genai-ort-sys-*/out/ort-prebuilt/lib
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure          # 3/3 PASS
# default fp32 vs int8 opt-in (8-tok gate + tok/s):
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ./build/mps_e2e <model>/model.onnx \
  "$PWD/build/libonnxruntime_mps_ep.dylib" tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 8      # gate PASS
ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_MATMUL_INT8=1 DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ./build/mps_e2e ... 8   # gate PASS
```

# MatMulNBits prefill GEMM (simdgroup_matrix MMA) — Metal now BEATS CPU on TTFT at 256/512-token prompts (unblocks the hybrid)

**By:** Mariette (Metal/MPS Kernel Engineer)
**Date:** 2026-07-13
**Machine:** Apple M1 Max, macOS 25.x (~400 GB/s theoretical UMA bandwidth)
**Repo:** `onnxruntime-mps` (Metal EP). Model: `onnx-genai/models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe/model.onnx`
(fp32 graph, 169 MatMulNBits, whole decoder = 1 fused subgraph).
**No commit — coordinator commits.**

## TL;DR

Batty measured (and I reproduced exactly) that Metal prefill/TTFT was **1.5–2× SLOWER than CPU,
gap growing with prompt length** — because the Metal `MatMulNBits` kernel was a **decode GEMV
replicated once per prompt row** (`grid.y = M`, no reuse): prefill re-streamed the full int4 weight
set M times = M×-weight-bandwidth-bound, the GPU's weakness.

I added a **tiled prefill GEMM** (`mps_matmulnbits_gemm_f32`) using **`simdgroup_matrix`
(simdgroup_float8x8) MMA** ops that loads each weight tile into threadgroup memory **once** and
reuses it across the M rows of the tile (compute-bound, where the GPU wins). Decode (M=1) is
untouched. Auto-routed for **M ≥ 8**.

Result — **Metal prefill now BEATS CPU at 256 and 512-token prompts** and is 1.7–2.2× faster than
the old GEMV-replicated prefill at every length. **This unblocks Batty's GPU-prefill/CPU-decode
hybrid** (the KV-handoff seam is already proven).

| prompt tokens | CPU TTFT | **Metal GEMM (NEW)** | old Metal GEMV | Metal/CPU | GEMM vs old GEMV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|:--:|:--:|
| 26   | ~33 ms   | **~57 ms**   | ~63 ms   | 1.73× (CPU) | 1.1× faster |
| 256  | ~276 ms  | **~242 ms**  | ~507 ms  | **0.88× — Metal FASTER** | 2.1× faster |
| 512  | ~570 ms  | **~560 ms**  | ~1099 ms | **0.98× — Metal FASTER** | 2.0× faster |
| 1024 | ~1271 ms | **~1522 ms** | ~2631 ms | 1.20× (CPU) | 1.7× faster |

(Best-of-N prefill-only forward, empty KV; my NOGEMM baseline reproduces Batty's old-Metal numbers
26/256/512/1024 = 66/525/1128/2756 ms to within thermals.) Metal wins the 256–512 sweet spot; at
26 it stays overhead-bound (tiny M), and at 1024 the remaining deficit is dominated by the O(M²)
attention (GQA) kernel, not MatMulNBits — a separate lever.

## The GEMM kernel (`src/kernels/matmulnbits.metal`, new `mps_matmulnbits_gemm_f32`)

Structure mirrors the Apple gold standard (llama.cpp `ggml-metal.metal` `kernel_mul_mm` +
`dequantize_q4_*`) — reimplemented, not vendored.

- **Tiling:** BM=32, BN=32, BK=32. Threadgroup = 128 threads = **4 simdgroups in a 2×2 grid**, each
  owning a 16×16 output subtile = **2×2 array of 8×8 fp32 accumulators**. Each staged weight tile is
  reused across all 32 rows of the tile ⇒ a length-M prefill reads the weight set ~**M/32 times**
  instead of M times.
- **K-loop = one quant block per step.** BK == block_size == 32, so each K-step maps to exactly one
  scale per column — clean dequant with no intra-tile block bookkeeping. Stage `As[32×32]` (fp16
  activations) and `Bs[32×32]` (fp16 **dequantized** weights, `(q−8)·scale`) into threadgroup memory
  cooperatively (128 threads), one `threadgroup_barrier` before the MMA and one after.
- **MMA:** `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(acc, Afrag, Bfrag, acc)`. `Bfrag` is loaded **transposed**
  so the 8×8 fragment is Bᵀ (indices `[k][n]`), giving `C[m,n] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B_deq[n,k]`. **fp16
  tiles, fp32 accumulate** (`simdgroup_float8x8`) — the llama.cpp precision recipe.
- **Store:** accumulators → threadgroup scratch → bounds-checked + bias copy-out to device. M/N need
  not be tile multiples (staging zero-pads; store bounds-checks).

**Tile sweep:** BM=64/BN=32 (the llama.cpp 8-accumulator layout) was measured **slower** here
(256: 314 vs 242 ms) — the extra register/threadgroup pressure cut occupancy more than the halved
weight traffic helped. **32×32 with 128 threads is the M1 occupancy sweet spot** and is kept.

## Dispatch selection (`src/ep/metal_context.{h,mm}`, `src/ep/ep.cc`)

- New `MatMulNBitsVariant::GemmF32`. In `MatMulNBitsF32`, `Auto` now routes **M ≥ threshold →
  GemmF32** (threadgroups `⌈N/32⌉ × ⌈M/32⌉`, 128 threads/group), else the tuned **VectorF32 GEMV**
  (decode, M=1). `ep.cc` passes the runtime M; **decode M=1 is byte-for-byte the same dispatch as
  before — untouched.**
- Env knobs: `ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_GEMM_THRESHOLD=<int>` (default 8);
  `ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_NOGEMM=1` forces the old GEMV-replicated prefill (for A/B measurement — this
  is how I reproduced the old numbers). Orthogonal to the existing `_SCALAR` / `_FP16` / `_INT8`
  knobs.

## Correctness (verified FIRST)

- **Per-kernel** (`tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc`, new `TestMatMulNBitsGemm`, target
  `mps_mariette_tests`): forces `GemmF32` at **M ∈ {8, 32, 128}** and at **ragged M/N** (40×96,
  100×48, 8×40 — not tile multiples, exercising the boundary padding + bounds-checked store) and
  **K up to 1088** (34 blocks). vs the fp32 CPU reference: **worst abs-err 0.00295, worst rel-err
  1.74 %** (|ref|≥0.1) — fp16-tile-bounded, well inside the combined atol+rtol gate.
- **ctest**: `mps_kernel_tests`, `mps_mariette_tests`, `mps_ort_reference_tests` → **3/3 PASS**.
- **E2E coherence** (`mps_e2e`, real 26-tok "capital of France" prompt, greedy, 8-tok gate):
  **PASS** — Metal stream `785 6722 315 9625 374 12095 13 151645` == CPU ("The capital of France is
  Paris."). At padded prompts the gate can show FAIL, but the **GEMM Metal stream is byte-identical
  to the old-GEMV Metal stream** (both diverge from CPU at the same token) — i.e. it is the known
  pre-existing Metal fp32-dequant vs CPU int8 `accuracy_level=4` drift, **not** a GEMM defect.

## Decode unchanged

M=1 routes to the same `VectorF32` GEMV (threshold 8) — the decode hot path and its ~133 tok/s
steady figure (`mariette-matmulnbits-bandwidth`) are untouched; no code in that kernel changed.

## Safety (post-leak-fix discipline)

The GEMM path adds **no new device allocation**: it reuses the already-resolved operand buffers
(weights are device-resident from `ep.cc`'s one-time `Alloc`, freed in `~MarietteKernel`; any
wrapped host temporaries are released by `RunPass` exactly as the other kernels). All GEMM scratch
is **static threadgroup memory** (auto, ~8 KB: As 2 KB + Bs 2 KB + Cs 4 KB) — no unbounded
allocation, no new `-release` obligation. Tested with **bounded** runs (4 prompt lengths, ≤3 prefill
iters, ≤8 decode tokens); no memory sweep.

## Handoff

- **Batty:** Metal prefill now beats CPU at 256/512 tokens — **re-run `hybrid_prefill_decode`**; the
  GPU-prefill/CPU-decode hybrid should now win total latency in that range (KV-handoff already
  proven + free).
- **Next Metal levers (not MatMulNBits):** the 1024-token residual deficit is the **O(M²) GQA
  attention** kernel (prefill flash-attention tiling) and the double-buffered command-buffer submit
  — profile with `ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_PROFILE`.

## Files changed (coordinator to commit — I did NOT commit)

- `src/kernels/matmulnbits.metal` — **new** `mps_matmulnbits_gemm_f32` (simdgroup_matrix MMA tiled
  prefill GEMM; fp16 tiles, fp32 accumulate; dequant-in-threadgroup).
- `src/ep/metal_context.mm` — register the pipeline; `Auto` M≥threshold → GemmF32 dispatch
  (threadgroups); `_GEMM_THRESHOLD` / `_NOGEMM` env knobs.
- `src/ep/metal_context.h` — `GemmF32` enum value + doc.
- `src/ep/ep.cc` — comment: prefill auto-routes on runtime M (no behavior change).
- `tests/kernels/mariette_kernel_test.cc` — new `TestMatMulNBitsGemm` (M=8/32/128 + ragged M/N vs
  fp32 ref).
- `tests/e2e/e2e_test.cc` — `MeasurePrefill` (warmup + best-of-N prefill/TTFT), `[pad_to]` +
  `[prefill_iters]` args (token-repeat padding for the length sweep), prefill/TTFT report line.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd onnxruntime-mps && cmake --build build -j8
ORTLIB=$(dirname $(ls <onnx-genai>/target/release/build/onnx-genai-ort-sys-*/out/ort-prebuilt/lib/libonnxruntime.dylib|head -1))
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure           # 3/3 PASS
MODEL=<onnx-genai>/models/qwen2.5-0.5b-cpu-recipe/model.onnx
EP=$PWD/build/libonnxruntime_mps_ep.dylib
# coherence gate (unpadded 26-tok):
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ./build/mps_e2e "$MODEL" "$EP" tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 8         # PASS
# TTFT sweep: mps_e2e <model> <ep> <tokens> <num_new> <pad_to> <prefill_iters>
for P in 0 256 512 1024; do
  DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ./build/mps_e2e "$MODEL" "$EP" tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 8 $P 4 | grep prefill/TTFT
done
# A/B vs old GEMV-replicated prefill:
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ORTLIB ONNX_GENAI_METAL_EP_NOGEMM=1 ./build/mps_e2e "$MODEL" "$EP" tests/e2e/prompt_tokens.txt 8 512 4
```
